title: Revealing Two Distinct Molecular Binding Modes inPolyethyleneimine-DNA Polyplexes using Infrared Spectroscopy
authors: Rusul Mustafa; Danielle Diorio; Madeline Harper; David Punihaole
one_liner_zh: 该文用红外光谱研究PEI-DNA复合物的分子结合模式，虽涉及DNA互作但非TF-DNA体系，且方法为光谱实验而非AI或物理模拟，与课题核心匹配度低。
abstract: In this study, we use infrared spectroscopy to investigate the molecular binding modes of DNA with linear and branched polyethylenimine (LPEI and BPEI). PEI-based polymers are widely studied as non-viral gene delivery vectors, but their low transfection efficiency limits their clinical success. One key factor affecting their performance is how they bind DNA as it directly impacts the packaging, protection, and release of the cargo in cells. While PEI-DNA binding has traditionally been viewed through the lens of electrostatics, computational models suggest additional binding mechanisms may be involved. Our findings reveal that LPEI and BPEI exhibit two distinct molecular binding modes, which influence DNA condensation. Identifying these unique interactions provides critical insights into polymer complexation mechanisms to nucleic acids that can guide the rational design of more efficient and versatile PEI-based gene delivery systems.
abstract_zh: 在本研究中，我们利用红外光谱技术探究DNA与线性和支化聚乙烯亚胺（LPEI和BPEI）的分子结合模式。基于PEI的聚合物作为非病毒基因递送载体被广泛研究，但其较低的转染效率限制了其临床成功。影响其性能的一个关键因素是它们如何与DNA结合，因为这直接影响到货物在细胞内的包装、保护和释放。虽然PEI-DNA结合传统上被视为通过静电作用，但计算模型提示可能涉及额外的结合机制。我们的研究结果表明，LPEI和BPEI表现出两种不同的分子结合模式，这些模式影响DNA的凝聚。识别这些独特相互作用为聚合物与核酸的复合机制提供了关键见解，可指导更高效、多功能的基于PEI的基因递送系统的合理设计。
